answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring every account to lock a bond before joining. Contracts and votes then depend on stake plus reputation earned through a long record of completed tasks. Random peers audit claims, and a failed audit or double-signing slashes the bond and lowers future earnings. A Sybil attacker must fund many bonds and reproduce honest work across many accounts; one detected fraud destroys capital. Thus cipher, zephyr, and whisper gain no cheap exemption from the same cost.
